clue.text: Gem presented to Bolivian city, the Spanish having left

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: having left says the Spanish article departs from the city's name

parts.note: La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia
la is the Spanish feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A jewel is handed over to a South American city once its Spanish inhabitants have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' removes LA from LA PAZ, leaving PAZ; 'presented' simply joins TO to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Topaz is a precious stone, usually yellow, so it is an example of a gem.

clue.text: Painter's thrown out pest spilling claret round university

indicators.note: thrown suggests the little word out is tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a louse is a parasitic insect, a pest

indicators.note: round says the rearranged wine wraps about the university letter
spilling suggests the wine's letters slop about into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a nuisance who has knocked red wine over a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' makes TOU and 'spilling' makes LATREC, which 'round' wraps about U. The 's means 'is', a link; the surface's wine-spilling pest is pure misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec was a French artist famous for his Montmartre posters, so he is a painter.

clue.text: Put forward final thought about old wine

indicators.note: about says the postscript letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a postscript, PS, is a final thought added to a letter
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Someone offers a last reflection on some vintage wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the postscript round O; IT is short for Italian vermouth, familiar from 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to propose or suggest an idea for consideration, which is to put it forward.

clue.text: Huge number indisposed to enter Christian Church

indicators.note: to enter says the sickly word goes inside the church

parts.note: Zion is used for the Christian Church or the heavenly city
indisposed means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Countless people too unwell to go into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' signals the container; Zion stands for the Church as the new Jerusalem in hymn and scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Zillion is an informal word for an indefinitely vast quantity, so it means a huge number.

clue.text: Purchase territory on the Gulf of Mexico?

definitions.text: Purchase territory on the Gulf of Mexico?

parts.words: Purchase territory on the Gulf of Mexico?
parts.note: read as a land bought by the United States from France in 1803, whose namesake state lies on the Gulf coast

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy some land beside the Gulf of Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1803 Purchase from France doubled the size of the USA; the modern state bearing that name borders the Gulf of Mexico. 'Purchase' looks like a verb but belongs to the historic name.
explanation.definitionFit: This US state lies on the Gulf of Mexico and gave its name to the huge 1803 land purchase.

clue.text: Face upwards, as tables may be?

indicators.note: upwards, in a down clue, says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: A request to turn something face up, the way tables are set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upwards' turns DIAL round to make LAID; tables are laid for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A table set ready for a meal with cloth and cutlery is said to be laid.

clue.text: Soft leather case hidden in extremely ugly chair covers

indicators.note: hidden in says the case goes inside the outer letters
extremely picks the first and last letters of the word ugly

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning soft
a holster is a leather case for a pistol

explanation.surface: A soft leather case tucked away inside some very ugly chair coverings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives U and Y, the first and last letters of 'ugly'; 'hidden in' puts P plus HOLSTER between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstery is the padding and fabric covering of chairs and sofas, so it means chair covers.

clue.text: Beetle initially scares holidaymaker

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word scares

parts.note: a camper is a holidaymaker staying in a tent or van

explanation.surface: An insect frightens someone on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like the insect but is the verb meaning to scurry. 'initially' takes S from 'scares'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle about is to hurry along quickly, and to scamper is to run with quick light steps.

clue.text: Splendid naval officer digesting book on English

indicators.note: digesting says the officer takes in the book letter

parts.note: an admiral is a senior naval officer

explanation.surface: A fine naval officer reads a book about English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digesting' puts B inside ADMIRAL; in this down clue 'on' places that above E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something admirable deserves high praise, much as something splendid is excellent and impressive.

clue.text: Odd Latin name tutee originally placed third from last

indicators.note: odd says these words are put into a strange new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of the word placed

explanation.surface: A pupil with a strange Latin name came third from bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' gives P from 'placed', which joins LATIN, NAME and TUTEE; 'Odd' rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antepenultimate means coming before the penultimate, so it is the third from the last.

clue.text: Letters in Sun — mischievous or concerned for others?

indicators.note: letters in says the word sun's letters are taken and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
elfish means impish, mischievous like an elf

explanation.surface: A question whether a mischievous correspondent to The Sun newspaper is actually altruistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters in' signals the rearrangement, making UNS. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper with a letters page, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An unselfish person puts others' needs before their own, being concerned for others.

clue.text: Acknowledge head of mine in entrance

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the entrance

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance to a mine

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word mine

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to the boss of a mine standing in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' gives M from 'mine'; 'in' puts it inside ADIT, a mining word for a horizontal passage into a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess or concede it, which is to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Business house's complete set of equipment

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a company or organisation
a full kit of gear or clothing for a purpose

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link meaning 'is', joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Outfit is informal for a firm or group, and also means a complete set of clothes or equipment.

clue.text: Conservative crony rejected gin following pretentious talk

indicators.note: rejected says the friend's word is turned back

parts.note: a pal is a crony, a close friend
a gin is a snare, a trap

explanation.surface: A Tory's mate turned down a drink, after some pompous chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink but means a snare. 'rejected' turns PAL into LAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is empty, showy nonsense meant to win applause, so it is pretentious talk.

clue.text: Much prized business held to be developing early

indicators.note: held says the company letters are held within the valued word

parts.note: something precious is much prized
CO is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: A highly valued firm is thought to be growing fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' signals the container; 'to be' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A precocious child shows abilities sooner than usual, so they are developing early.

clue.text: Silk distributor determined to secure place near Harrow

indicators.note: to secure says the determined word holds the place inside it

parts.note: set means determined, as in set on doing something
Pinner is a district of north-west London next to Harrow

explanation.surface: A silk merchant is resolved to get premises near Harrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to secure' signals the container. Pinner and Harrow are neighbouring suburbs of north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinneret is the organ through which a spider or silkworm releases silk thread, so it distributes silk.

clue.text: Little devil's deed, produces forcible contact

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
an action is a deed

explanation.surface: A mischievous sprite's act causes a collision.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is possessive on the surface but just joins IMP to ACTION; 'produces' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaction is the act of pressing or striking firmly together, a forcible contact.

clue.text: Hood, possibly, no good in ceremonial dressing?

indicators.note: no says the good letter is to be left out

parts.note: robing is the putting on of ceremonial robes

explanation.surface: A question whether a hood without quality belongs in formal attire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like a garment, fitting the dressing surface, but is the outlaw. 'no' removes G from ROBING.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest, so Hood is one example of a Robin.

clue.text: Bounded along, and cut back half-heartedly

indicators.note: half-heartedly says one of the two central letters is lost, halving the heart

parts.note: lopped means cut back, as branches are

explanation.surface: Someone hopped along and pruned without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' removes one of the two Ps at the centre of LOPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long easy strides, so having loped is having bounded along.

clue.text: Ted's abandoned firmly established type of fishing

indicators.note: abandoned says the name is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: deep-seated means firmly established
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ted has given up a well-rooted fishing habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' removes TED from DEEP-SEATED; the 's means 'is', the link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea fishing is angling in deep offshore waters, so deep-sea names a type of fishing.

clue.text: It's performed by acrobat, one that's on the wagon

definitions.meaning: a gymnastic sideways handspring that an acrobat does
a wheel fitted to a cart

explanation.walkthrough: 'on the wagon' suggests teetotal, but here it is literal: one of the wagon's wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartwheel is both an acrobatic sideways somersault and the wheel of a cart.

clue.text: Time little Scots fellow died?

parts.note: wee means little, especially in Scotland
Ken is a common Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A question whether a small Scotsman has passed away.
explanation.definitionFit: A weekend is the period of Saturday and Sunday, a span of time.

clue.text: Loosen grip on relative's new companion

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone eases their hold on a family member's new partner.
explanation.walkthrough: CH, Companion of Honour, is a British award; the 's on relative's is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclench a fist or jaw is to relax it, so it means loosen grip on.

clue.text: Asian friend in centre of Newcastle, giving address

indicators.note: in says the friend goes inside the address code

parts.note: NE1 is the postcode for central Newcastle upon Tyne, with the digit read as the letter I
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: An Asian friend in the middle of Newcastle hands over an address.
explanation.walkthrough: UK postcodes begin with area letters; NE1 covers the centre of Newcastle, and 1 is read as I. 'in' puts PAL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a person from Nepal, a Himalayan country, so a Nepali is Asian.

clue.text: Where Lucy Ashton was led to change, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A heroine was taken somewhere for a transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucy Ashton is the heroine of Walter Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor, led to the altar to marry against her will.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride is led up the aisle to the table in church where the wedding takes place.

clue.text: Evidence of injury produced panic out East

indicators.note: out says the compass letter is removed

parts.note: a scare is a panic

explanation.surface: A mark of a wound caused alarm in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from SCARE; 'produced' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on skin after a wound heals, evidence of injury.

clue.text: Controls are insupportable? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely says the answer is only part of the words are insupportable

explanation.surface: A question whether controls are completely unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' signals a run of letters inside 'are insupportable'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are the straps used to steer a horse, and figuratively means of control.

clue.text: Players unmatched in Scotland, bringing in funds

indicators.note: bringing in says the Scots word takes the funds inside

parts.note: orra is a Scots word for odd or unmatched
a chest is a fund of money, as in a war chest

explanation.surface: Unrivalled Scottish performers attract money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' signals the container. Orra is a Scots word meaning odd or unpaired, little known outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a band of musicians, so it is a group of players.

clue.text: One stands to gain from this person's soliciting

definitions.text: One stands to gain from this person's soliciting

parts.words: One stands to gain from this person's soliciting
parts.note: read as a candidate standing for election who benefits from a helper going door to door seeking votes

explanation.walkthrough: 'One stands' means a candidate stands for office; 'soliciting' is asking for votes, not anything shadier.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvasser goes round asking people for their votes on behalf of a candidate.

clue.text: Funeral song, for example, delivered by return

indicators.note: by return says the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: rid means delivered or freed

explanation.surface: A song for a funeral is sent back in the post, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by return' turns EGRID round to give DIRGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament sung at a funeral.
